settings.challenge_description:
The challenge was to strike a balance between sophisticated and approachable.

I wanted the home to feel elevated but never overly formal, where you could host a dinner party, but also curl up with a blanket and a good book.
settings.project_description:
This home was designed to feel calm, curated, and collected – with warm layers, timeless neutrals, and thoughtful textures throughout. I wanted it to be a place that felt elevated but never overly formal. Every corner was created with purpose, balancing open airy moments with cozy, intimate nooks.

Coziology's window treatments played a huge role in pulling that vision together, adding softness, texture, light control, and a level of finish that instantly made each room feel complete.

settings.title: Design Process and Collaboration with Cozyology
settings.description:
Design Philosophy:

My approach always centers on designing spaces that feel collected and calming. I gravitate toward neutral tones, layered textures, and furnishings that are both classic and current.

For this home, I leaned into that mindset - building the foundation with timeless pieces and layering in decor and accents that brought personality and interest.

Cozyology’s drapes were an easy decision. Their quality, customization options, and overall aesthetic aligned seamlessly with the look and feel I envisioned.
settings.info: From the start, I knew I wanted continuity throughout the home—but with slight variations to keep each room feeling unique. I love using the same material across multiple spaces, but changing up the color, style, or light filtering to align with the intended function and mood.

settings.title: Challenges Overcome with Cozyology Curtains
settings.content:
The Primary Bedroom had soaring ceilings that initially felt more vast than inviting. It’s a space where you want to feel cozy and relaxed, but the scale was throwing it off.

We solved this by hanging full-length drapes from ceiling to floor, with extra width on each side to frame the window to add softness.

It completely changed the feel of the room—so much cozier, and visually balanced.

settings.title: Dining Room
settings.description: I used the Liam Linen Pleated Drapes in Morning Mist, unlined, to keep the space soft and airy while still adding texture to the neutral palette.

settings.title: Office
settings.description:
I went with Liam Linen Roman Shades in Morning Mist, which felt like the perfect
tailored-but-cozy final touch.

settings.title: Bedroom
settings.description: I chose the blackout version in Ivory Cream. They look so luxurious and I no longer have to listen to my husband complaining about the early morning sun, which is an added bonus!

settings.title: About the Designer
settings.introduce:
Shay Miron is an Atlanta-based interior designer known for her thoughtful use of layered neutrals, refined textures, and focus on functional design.

She brings a sense of calm to every project, with an eye for detail and a passion for creating spaces that feel elevated yet personal.

Her designs focus on timeless styling that prioritizes function and comfort - proof that luxury doesn’t have to feel untouchable.
settings.reason:
I chose Cozyology because they make the process of sourcing custom window treatments feel easy and accessible.

Their craftsmanship is top-tier, their fabrics are beautiful, and they offer the kind of flexibility you need when designing multiple spaces.

Every pleat, every finish,every detail—they get it right.

settings.title: Designer’s Takeaways
settings.takeaways:
Key Design Lessons:
We often hear that when choosing window treatments, or anything in a home, it’s important to focus on both form and function.

Cozyology’s products are not only beautiful but also highly functional. They help manage light, maintain privacy, and create the perfect mood for each room.

I always say, a room is never fully complete until the windows are dressed.

When designing a space, we obsess over tile grout and faucet finishes, but often treat the one element that actually controls how the room feels as an afterthought. Drapes or shades can change the whole mood of a room, so don’t overlook them in your projects."
